skills_invoked: {"skill": "team-ops-delivery:plan-forecast-recovery", "args": "Solo builder, interrupt-heavy support plus feature queue. Wants a lightweight delivery rhythm (no meetings, no Scrum roles) and asks whether WIP / throughput can be used as an 85th-percentile promise."}

judge.reason: The answer says WIP÷throughput is Little's Law, which gives a long-run average in a stable system rather than a P85. It says to build the SLE from actual cycle-time history once there are 15–20 items per type, labels anything less as a guess, and asks for real start and finish dates rather than inventing numbers. It also gives a meeting-free pull rhythm (finish the oldest item first, an interrupt lane, explicit WIP caps, weekly re-ranking by value) with no Scrum roles or ceremonies; the one mild gap is that the weekly review looks at throughput and aging rather than at the outcomes delivered work produced.
